source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check Language options in Login page.
2. Check Language in each page.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Language should support English, Spanish and Russian.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- "Language": the BMC web language/settings display preference. Agent can read the current language setting via browser, changing it is state-changing and must be confirmed.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the current UI language setting (before/after if changed) so user confirms it is correct.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: changing the UI language is a preference change; confirm the desired language and revert after.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes a browser and stateful preference, but narrows the case to reading/changing one setting. It omits the explicit English/Spanish/Russian option set, `each page` coverage, translation accuracy/completeness, layout, dynamic messages, preference scope and protected evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly restores the three-language page matrix, references, endpoint/build identity, preference rollback and human translation judgment. This review retains that classification and defines coverage and fallback checkpoints.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 839/2291 preserves PARTIAL but incorrectly locates the browser check at a DUT host over SSH and leaves runtime validation unspecified; the observation and mutation surface is the BMC web UI.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1002 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 treats language references, page matrix and environment as readiness inputs rather than permanent blockage; ED-38 requires approval for state change, restoration, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC web login page offers English, Spanish and Russian and, after selecting each language, every Project-required page, control, status, validation/error and dynamic message renders in the selected language without missing, fallback, clipped or corrupted text.
original_method: Bind the exact BMC/UI build and initial language; inspect the login selector; select English, Spanish and Russian one at a time; traverse an approved page/message matrix; compare extracted and rendered text with authoritative translations and layout rules; record defects; then restore the original or approved final preference and verify its scope.
manual_activity: An engineer/localization owner supplies the authoritative translations, page/message/role matrix, preference scope and layout tolerances, approves changing the setting and adjudicates linguistic/contextual correctness. Browser automation can execute navigation, extract strings, compare references and capture evidence after approval.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC identity, firmware/web UI bundle and trusted URL/certificate
Exact supported locale identifiers for English, Spanish and Russian, default/fallback behavior and customer/vendor translation references
Login-page and post-login page/navigation matrix by account role, including dialogs, validation/errors, asynchronous notifications, empty/loading states and help text
Expected date/time/number/unit formatting, character encoding, font/glyph coverage, wrapping/clipping/overflow and acceptable untranslated technical terms
Supported browser/version, viewport/device scale/zoom, theme and browser Accept-Language/default locale
Whether preference is anonymous-session, cookie, per-user or global; initial value, active-user impact, approved test accounts, sequence and restoration path
Protected credentials/session handling, screenshot/DOM redaction and authorized language reviewers
safety_requirements: Do not change the language until endpoint/build, preference scope, active-user impact, baseline and rollback are approved; do not assume the selection is only local to one browser.
Use dedicated approved accounts/sessions where possible and never overwrite another operator's global or per-user preference without consent.
Protect credentials, cookies, tokens, hostnames, serials and customer data in screenshots, DOM dumps, network traces and browser storage.
Do not clear BMC or system logs; log deletion is unrelated and destroys the baseline.
Do not accept selector labels or a current-setting readback as proof that each required page supports all three languages.

Do not use simple string presence alone as a translation verdict; verify context, interpolation/plurals, fallback language, glyphs, wrapping/clipping, layout and locale-sensitive values against approved references.
Record inaccessible pages and role-dependent coverage rather than silently skipping them; one account role cannot prove `each page` if other roles expose unique content.

Restore and independently re-read/reload the approved final preference. Do not automatically retry failed mutation/navigation; preserve first-failure state and obtain direction if rollback or access is uncertain.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, verify target/build, enumerate language options and page/routes without changing preference, record baseline/scope and prepare the exact role/page/message matrix.
After approval, select each of English, Spanish and Russian once per defined scope, reload as required and navigate every accessible approved matrix cell in a controlled browser.

Extract visible DOM/accessibility text, compare normalized message identifiers/references, test locale-sensitive values and capture redacted screenshots for rendering, glyph and layout defects; keep raw source strings where available.
Restore the original or approved final preference, verify it through a new load/session as specified, report untested cells and facts only, and do not issue the engineer's verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve locale definitions, authoritative translations, role/page/state matrix, browser contexts, allowed untranslated terms and visual/linguistic tolerances.
Approve preference changes and rollback after confirming whether the setting is session, cookie, per-user or global and assessing active-user impact.
Review machine-reported missing/fallback/layout defects and visually/linguistically adjudicate contextual correctness before issuing the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The browser/preference concept is relevant, but its current-setting before/after evidence covers neither all three required languages nor `each page`; it also lacks target identity, references, preference scope, role matrix, protected sessions and verified restoration.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use an approved browser automation profile bound to the target build. Record the baseline, change one locale at a time only after approval, traverse the complete role/page/state matrix, compare DOM/accessibility text and screenshots against references, then restore and verify the approved final value.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: English, Spanish and Russian, login-page options, each-page inspection, no Script and 5/0-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Identity/baseline preflight; approved preference sequence; automated role/page/state traversal for en/es/ru; string, fallback, formatting and rendering analysis; human localization review; verified restore.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC firmware/web UI bundle, supported account roles and browser rendering environments.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/UI build, translation catalog/version or asset hashes, browser/OS/viewport and locale settings.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor localization catalog, customer terminology and page/role coverage matrix; generic browser locale behavior cannot define expected translations.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Expands `check each page` into an auditable cross-product of locale, role, page and dynamic state while preserving the required languages and reversible preference change.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A selector or current setting is partial evidence; static pages do not cover errors/dynamic content; one role cannot cover all pages; automated string equality cannot alone judge linguistic quality or visual fit.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Endpoint/build, catalogs, matrix, preference scope, browser contexts, accounts, security, rollback and reviewers.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Language mutation may affect other sessions; automated traversal may miss conditional states; screenshots can expose data; reference catalogs can lag the deployed build.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC defines locale identifiers, translation/catalog version, account-role page matrix and whether additional or fewer languages are in scope. Any Project Override must preserve the source requirement for English, Spanish and Russian unless an engineer explicitly records why coverage differs and which locale/page cells remain unverified.
expected_evidence: BMC endpoint/certificate identity, firmware/UI build, translation catalog/reference version and browser/rendering metadata
Login selector evidence listing English, Spanish and Russian with locale codes and initial preference/scope
Completed locale × role × page × state matrix with navigation result, extracted strings/message IDs, fallback/untranslated-string report and locale-sensitive value checks
Redacted screenshots for representative and every defect-bearing cell showing glyphs, wrapping, clipping, alignment and language state
Preference write/read/reload audit for each locale, original/final restoration in a clean session, health result, untested cells and authorized localization/engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require English, Spanish and Russian support at login and across the BMC web pages. `Each page` needs a Project-defined inventory, but this is a supplyable coverage input rather than a competing purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The language options and broad page-validation objective are clear. Endpoint/build, catalog, page/role matrix, test accounts, preference scope and rollback can be supplied for execution; missing values are readiness pending, not a permanent contradiction.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its reduction to current-setting readback and restores the full three-language, each-page functional coverage with controlled mutation and rollback.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation, references, page matrix, protected browser evidence and restoration; adds role/state cross-product, fallback, interpolation and locale-format evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Corrects the location from DUT-host/SSH to the BMC browser UI and replaces deferred sanity with an explicit localization matrix.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a visible language menu or one successful preference change from being accepted while pages, roles, errors or dynamic messages remain untranslated, clipped or stuck in fallback English.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source's `each page` wording makes this a functional localization matrix, not a read-only preference inspection. Browser automation can traverse routes and detect missing/fallback strings and layout defects, but changing the preference is stateful and linguistic/contextual correctness depends on approved references and human review. That combination fits package/user confirmation and preserves the original coverage instead of downgrading it to read-only.
